unharnessed.meaning: Every step survives with quantities intact: "three-quarters of a pound of fat salt pork", "every half inch, making the cuts an inch deep", "taking the lid off for the last hour". "some poor bugger broke the bean pot" adds a person to the broken pot, colour hanging off the original.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "Snags" for sausages, "go in the bin", "chuck the bean water outside", "whack it in the bottom", "the beans go down easier on the guts" for more easily digested. "bake it low and slow" is exact for "bake slowly".
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian reading the recipe out: "Lid on the bean pot, into the oven", "leaving the rind poking out", "Plenty of folks swear". Natural throughout.
unharnessed.register: Solidly casual and Aussie with "bloody good" and "poor bugger", but it stays a recipe rather than a full pub yarn; vulgarity well within 2. A shade under level 5.
unharnessed.tone: Practical instructions stay practical; the dry closing note about the lard pail keeps its wry edge: "where some poor bugger broke the bean pot and used a five-pound lard bucket instead".
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "Tip the beans in the pot and bury the pork in 'em, leaving the rind poking out." No pile-ups.
unharnessed.variety: Varied verbs and tags: "chuck", "whack", "tip", "top up", "poking out"; "bloody good" appears twice ("The bloody good name", "bloody good baked").
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the 1896 recipe, with its quirky tested-beans rule and the lard-pail aside intact.

yarn.meaning: Every step and quantity survives: "one-quarter inch slice", "every one-half inch, makin' the cuts one inch deep", "takin' the lid off for the last hour". "cos the bean-pot was cactus" renders the broken pot.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "the bean-pot was cactus" (broken), "scoffed" (eaten), "swear blind" (feel sure), "go down a fair bit easier on the gut". "The bonza name" is a slightly odd fit for a reputation.
yarn.authenticity: Natural Aussie: "whack it in the oven", "got pressed into service cos the bean-pot was cactus". "bonza" and "beaut" lean a touch dated-stock.
yarn.register: Casual and Aussie, more dialect than A with g-dropping throughout, but still a recipe rather than a pub yarn; one "bloody good". A shade under level 5.
yarn.tone: Practical instructions stay practical; the lard-pail aside keeps its wry note.
yarn.flow: Readable, but the g-dropping is relentless and a little clunky: "add one cup boilin' water", "makin' the cuts", "leavin' the rind showin'", "the seasonin's".
yarn.variety: Good spread: "bonza", "beaut", "cactus", "scoffed", "swear blind", "chucked out"; the dropped-g device is leaned on.
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the original recipe, quirks intact.

engine.meaning: Every step survives because the original is almost entirely kept word for word; "in which they're reckoned to be cooked" shifts "supposed" slightly but harmlessly.
engine.sense: Two strained terms: "Beans thus tested must, too right, be chucked away" uses "too right" (emphatic agreement) for "of course" (as a matter of course); "flamin' beaut when baked" is an odd fit for "very good".
engine.authenticity: Aussie tokens dropped into 1896 recipe prose: "must, too right, be chucked away", "chuckin' bean-water outta doors, not in sink", "'ave gained's been attributed". Stagey.
engine.register: Far under level 5: most of the text is the original ("Many feel sure that by adding with seasonings one-half tablespoon mustard, the beans are more easily digested."), with "Snags", a few g-drops and "beaut".
engine.tone: The instructional tone survives since the text is mostly unchanged; the inserted "too right" and "flamin' beaut" add a jarring jokiness in spots.
engine.flow: Clunky joins: "'ave gained's been attributed", "small top'n bulgin' sides", "must, too right, be chucked away".
engine.variety: Little to vary: "chucked"/"chuckin'" and "beaut" twice ("Equally beaut beans", "flamin' beaut").
engine.essence: Recognisably the recipe, since it is mostly left as written.

yarn.why: Dropped-g spellings are applied mechanically throughout and clutter the reading.

yarn.original: The fine reputation which Boston Baked Beans have gained

engine.quote: Beans thus tested must, too right, be chucked away.
engine.original: Beans thus tested must, of course, be thrown away.
engine.why: 'Too right' is emphatic agreement, not 'of course' as an aside; wrong sense and broken rhythm.

engine.quote: The fine reputation which Boston Baked Beans 'ave gained's been attributed
engine.original: The fine reputation which Boston Baked Beans have gained has been attributed
engine.why: Dialect contractions forced into formal prose produce an unreadable join.

engine.original: Many feel sure that by adding with seasonings one-half tablespoon mustard, the beans are more easily digested.
engine.why: Left untranslated; typical of most of the text, far under a level-5 brief.

engine.original: Yellow-eyed beans are very good when baked.

summaries.unharnessed: A natural, faithful casual-Aussie recipe; a shade under a full level-5 yarn.
summaries.yarn: A natural, faithful Aussie recipe with lively slang; heavy-handed g-dropping and a couple of stock words.
summaries.engine: Mostly the original with a few Aussie tokens, one wrong-sense 'too right' and clunky contractions; far under the brief.
